observed_title: Four Talagrand inequalities under the same umbrella
version: arXiv:1909.00363v1, 2019-09-01, 35 PDF pages; note/review version, not the original source of the four inequalities.

read_ranges.scope: entire note: original inequality statements, entropy duality/tensorization, log-Sobolev and hypercontractivity proofs, Gaussian Herbst argument, product-space convex-distance proof, L1-L2 variance proof, quadratic transport proof, empirical-process proof with truncation, discussion and complete references

topic_relevance.K05: direct overview/source map. It explicitly separates (i) standard-Gaussian Lipschitz concentration, (ii) Talagrand convex-distance concentration on arbitrary product probability spaces, (iii) the discrete-cube L1–L2 variance inequality, (iv) Gaussian quadratic transport-entropy, and (v) empirical-process supremum bounds. The review is a proof-bearing secondary source; it is not the original publication of those inequalities.

definitions.name: standard Gaussian concentration (equation (5))
definitions.statement: For standard Gaussian γ on R^n and Euclidean L-Lipschitz F, γ{F≥∫F dγ+r}≤exp(−r²/(2L²)) for r≥0. Applying the one-sided result to −F and taking a union bound gives γ{|F−∫F dγ|≥r}≤2exp(−r²/(2L²)).

definitions.name: product-space convex distance
definitions.statement: For P=⊗_i μ_i, the convex distance d_A(x) is Euclidean distance of 0 from the convex hull of mismatch-indicator vectors to A. The original inequality is represented as P(A) E_P exp(d_A(X)^2/4)≤1; the paper also derives a weaker-constant entropy-method proof and Lipschitz/convex corollaries.

definitions.name: four non-equivalent Talagrand inequalities
definitions.statement: The note separately states product convex-distance, discrete-cube L1–L2 variance, Gaussian quadratic transport-entropy, and empirical-process supremum inequalities; the shared entropy/log-Sobolev/hypercontractive proof principle does not make their hypotheses or outputs interchangeable.

theorem_cards.label: Equation (5) / Gaussian concentration from the Gross log-Sobolev inequality
assumptions: X has standard Gaussian law γ on R^n.
F:R^n→R is Euclidean L-Lipschitz; the theorem is around its Gaussian mean.
theorem_cards.statement: For r≥0, P(F(X)−E F(X)≥r)≤exp(−r²/(2L²)); hence P(|F(X)−EF(X)|≥r)≤2exp(−r²/(2L²)).
proof_steps: Prove the Gaussian logarithmic Sobolev inequality Entγ(f²)≤2∫|∇f|²dγ, with sharp constant 2.
Apply it to f=e^(λF/2) for smooth bounded 1-Lipschitz F to obtain E e^(λF)≤exp(λEF+λ²/2).
Approximate general Lipschitz F by Ornstein–Uhlenbeck smoothing and truncation.
Use Chernoff optimization λ=r/L² for the one-sided tail; apply the same to −F and union-bound for the two-sided form.
gaps: The result uses standard Gaussian measure and the Euclidean Lipschitz norm. It is not an inequality for arbitrary dependent laws or arbitrary convex functions without a concentration property of the input measure.
No claim of sharp numerical constants is made for the other three Talagrand inequalities in this review.

theorem_cards.label: Talagrand convex-distance inequality for product measures (original form summarized in Section 1)
assumptions: P=⊗_i μ_i is a product probability measure on a product measurable space.
A is measurable and nonempty; d_A is the convex distance defined from coordinate mismatch indicators.
theorem_cards.statement: P(A) E_P[exp(d_A(X)^2/4)]≤1 (equivalently E exp(d_A²/4)≤1/P(A)); the review’s entropy proof obtains an explicitly weaker numerical version and notes sharper constants/source formulations separately.
proof_steps: Show d_A equals sup over nonnegative unit ℓ² weights a of the weighted Hamming distance to A.
Use entropy tensorization and coordinate sensitivity to bound Ent_P(e^(λd_A²)).
Integrate the resulting Herbst differential inequality for positive and negative λ, using the single-coordinate squared-distance change bound.
Convert the Laplace transform estimate into the convex-distance tail/moment inequality.
gaps: The review explicitly makes no attempt to recover the sharp constant in the original inequality using its presented entropy proof; its original-form statement and its proof constants must not be conflated.

theorem_cards.label: Talagrand quadratic transportation-cost inequality (Gaussian case)
assumptions: γ is standard Gaussian on R^n.
μ=fγ is a probability measure with finite relative entropy and finite second moment.
proof_steps: Use Kantorovich duality with Hopf–Lax infimal convolution Q_sφ.
Apply the entropy variational inequality and Gaussian log-Sobolev inequality to e^(sQ_sφ).
Take the supremum in the dual formula.
gaps: This is transport-entropy for Gaussian measure, not the product convex-distance inequality or a generic Lipschitz-tail bound.

constant_dependence.explicit: Gaussian one-sided exponent is r²/(2L²); two-sided adds factor 2. For the Gaussian transport inequality the sharp coefficient is 2. The original product convex-distance statement has exponent coefficient 1/4 in exp(d_A²/4) and reciprocal P(A); the secondary proof’s constants are weaker. The empirical-process bound has dimension-free numerical constants and mixed Gaussian/Poisson regimes.
constant_dependence.dependence: Gaussian concentration depends only on Euclidean Lipschitz constant, not n. The product convex distance depends on product structure and its mismatch geometry. The four classes have distinct inputs/outputs and are not interchangeable.

endpoint_limits.measure: Gaussian concentration applies to standard Gaussian law; extensions require a separately established log-Sobolev/concentration property.
endpoint_limits.center: Source theorem is centered at the mean; a median-centered two-sided inequality follows only with additional conversion/constants, not by silently replacing mean with median.
endpoint_limits.product: Talagrand convex distance requires a product probability measure and the specified convex distance.
endpoint_limits.constants: The note says it does not optimize constants except the Gaussian transport coefficient; its proof-derived constants must not be attributed as sharp original constants.

reusable_methods.method: Gaussian log-Sobolev → Herbst Laplace transform → Chernoff tail
reusable_methods.transfer: For a candidate random statistic F(X), first prove X is standard Gaussian (or prove an appropriate LSI for its actual law) and establish Euclidean Lipschitz constant L; then the displayed Gaussian exponent applies. This is not an automatic statement for the center-cube maximal operator under dependent data.

reusable_methods.method: Product entropy tensorization and coordinate sensitivity
reusable_methods.transfer: Could be adapted only if input coordinates are independent under a product measure and the statistic has the required coordinate sensitivity/mismatch geometry; overlapping cube statistics do not themselves imply independence.

reusable_methods.method: Separate Talagrand variants by measure and output
reusable_methods.transfer: Choose Gaussian tails, product convex-distance, L1–L2 variance, transport-entropy or empirical-supremum inequality based on its own assumptions; do not transfer by surname or shared historical name.

unchecked: All 35 extracted pages, including proofs of the Gaussian concentration implication, product convex-distance, discrete-cube L1–L2, Gaussian transportation, and empirical-process inequality, were read. Equation (5) on PDF page 4 was visually checked in a PyMuPDF render.

I did not independently reprove the referenced original Talagrand theorems; the exact source here is the 2019 proof-bearing review by Michel Ledoux (P-b7ea4e1f39a3af1b, arXiv:1909.00363v1). Original references are explicitly listed in its References section.
